messages.author: 5a91d3696b12d600
messages.subject: Long run times for openCR
parts:
I am running a rather large model in openCR (33 parameters) to estimate survival and recruitment for 13 years of CMR data.  I am on iteration #4800 and the log likelihood has not changed for the past 1000 iterations.  Should I let it continue to run?  The parameter estimates are changing slightly over the last few hundred iterations but not by much.  Thanks for any advice!
Joe

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Long run times for openCR
parts:
Hi Joe
I don't have an answer, I'm afraid. I assume this is a spatial model and has taken forever? Someone should research strategies for large datasets. I have some myself that are too long to be practical in one sweep, hence the (unproven) function moving.fit(). No doubt a Bayesian approach would work, partly because it is less fussy about finding a unique solution. With that in mind, it seems reasonable to accept an almost-maximized ML result. You could carefully save the betas and use them as starting values for openCR.fit with method = 'none' to get variances etc. (see deep in the help for openCR.fit).
Murray
